Bond

A bond is money a tenant pays at the start of a tenancy. It is held by Tenancy Services as security in case the tenant does not meet their obligations under the tenancy agreement.

How much bond can a landlord ask for

A landlord can ask for a bond of up to four weeks' rent. The landlord cannot ask for more than this amount, even if the tenant agrees to pay it.

Lodging the bond

The landlord must lodge the bond with Tenancy Services within 23 working days of receiving it. Failing to lodge a bond is an unlawful act and the landlord may have to pay compensation.

Getting the bond back

At the end of the tenancy, the landlord and tenant fill in a bond refund form. If they disagree about how the bond should be paid out, either party can apply to the Tenancy Tribunal.
